# Ai Alerts

Human-readable reference generated from the same rules as the NewHeap consumer skills.

## Contents

- [Warn people about an object with alerts of a kind declared in code, raised by rules and by the application without a proposal](#warn-people-about-an-object-with-alerts-of-a-kind-declared-in-code-raised-by-rules-and-by-the-application-without-a-proposal)

## Warn people about an object with alerts of a kind declared in code, raised by rules and by the application without a proposal

Declare each kind of alert in code with AddAlertKind, let an agent's rules raise and resolve the kinds it lists with WithAlerts and ResolveAlerts, raise them from the application's code with INhAssistantAlerts, and rely on one open alert per kind, subject and key, on the recipient check before anything reaches a person, on expiry and on the bounded retention; the run maintenance delivers them immediately or in one daily digest per person in their time zone through Web Push, the in-app notifications and the application's channels, as each person chose per kind. People read, dismiss and count their own alerts through GET alerts with nh-assistant-alerts, the badge service and nh-assistant-notification-preferences. Administrators switch a kind off and change its default delivery within the bounds its code sets, and read its numbers, through GET and PUT admin/alert-kinds and the Alerts section of nh-assistant-admin. An agent's language model raises a kind only through the template its code declares with RaisedByModel, by the platform tool raise_alert in its own runs on one subject, with typed parameters the platform checks as plain values before anything is stored, once an administrator switched the kind on for the agent, first in shadow, through admin/agents/{id}/alert-model and the agent's Rollout tab.

## Preferred approach

Use an alert when an agent or the application must warn a person about an object and there is
nothing to approve: "your task is due today", "the document's deadline is in three days". An
alert never changes data, is never a proposal and grants nothing. When the agent should change
something, propose it instead (see the agent runs rule).

Declare every kind in code with `AddAlertKind(id, kind => ...)`. A kind needs a front-end
translation key for its name (`DisplayName`) and a `Title`, written from the alert's named
parameters per culture as `Func<CultureInfo, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>, string>`; add a
`Text` for more than a title. The platform asks for the texts with the reader's culture current
whenever it shows or delivers the alert, and once when the alert is raised, which a title that
fails or is empty refuses with `assistant-alert-text-invalid`. Keep the texts in the application's
resources, as SPM-392 does, so every language follows the translations. Give the kind an
`Urgency` (`Info`, `Warning`, `Urgent`), its recipients with `NhAssistantAlertRecipients`
(`SubjectResponsible`, `Explicit`, `SubjectApprovers` and `SubjectMembers(minRole)`, combined with
`Or`), an optional
`RepeatAfter` and its default `Delivery`: immediately, one `DailyDigest(time)` with
`WorkdaysOnly()`, and `ImmediatelyFrom(urgency)` for alerts that cannot wait. Declare what a person
may change with `PersonMayChange` (`Mute`, `DigestTime`, `Channels`), or make the kind `Required()`
so nobody mutes it. `PushShows` stays `TitleOnly` unless the text is safe on a lock screen.

```csharp
assistant
    .AddAlertKind("task-due-today", kind => kind
        .DisplayName("app.alerts.task-due-today")
        .Urgency(NhAssistantAlertUrgency.Warning)
        .Title((culture, parameters) => Texts.Format("TaskDueToday", culture, parameters["task"]))
        .Recipients(NhAssistantAlertRecipients.SubjectResponsible.Or(NhAssistantAlertRecipients.Explicit))
        .RepeatAfter(TimeSpan.FromDays(1))
        .Delivery(delivery => delivery.DailyDigest(new TimeOnly(7, 30)).WorkdaysOnly().ImmediatelyFrom(NhAssistantAlertUrgency.Urgent)))
    .ConfigureAgent("deadline-watch", agent => agent
        .UseRuleHandler<DeadlineWatchRules>()
        .Alerts("task-due-today"));
```

An agent lists the kinds its rules may raise with `Alerts(...)`; startup refuses a kind that is not
registered. Rules raise alerts with `NhAssistantRuleResult.Done(...).WithAlerts(...)` and resolve them
with `ResolveAlerts(...)`; both apply when the rules end. A rule result that raises or resolves a kind
its agent does not list fails the run with `assistant-alert-kind-not-listed` and applies none of its
alerts, so the mistake shows in the runs view instead of silently warning nobody. A paused or stopped
agent raises nothing (it still resolves), and a shadow agent or shadow run records shadow alerts that
reach nobody. The application's own code raises and resolves alerts without an agent through
`INhAssistantAlerts.RaiseAsync` and `ResolveAsync`, which return `TaskResult` with the stable codes of
`NhAssistantAlertCodes`.

An alert carries its kind, its subject, a `Key`, bounded string `Parameters`, optional explicit
`Recipients` and an optional `ExpiresAt`; its subject is its link, which the host routes as it routes
the subject. One open alert exists per kind, subject and key: raise the same alert every round and let
the platform deduplicate. Raising it again with new content updates it in place as its next revision;
it reaches people again only when its urgency rises or after the kind's `RepeatAfter`, and never a
person who dismissed it until the key changes. Choose the key so that it changes exactly when people
should hear about it again, for example the due date. Resolve an alert when its reason is gone, or
give it an expiry; a resolved or expired alert takes back the deliveries that did not go out, and the
run maintenance purges closed alerts after `NhAssistantLimits.AlertRetention` (30 days by default).

Every recipient is checked before anything reaches them, when the alert is raised, delivered and read:
the person exists, the application's principal factory still rebuilds them for the subject in its
division or tenant, and the subject's resolver gives them at least `Reader`, or the role of a kind that
selects only members (see below). Anyone else is left out
with the content-free audit `AgentAlertRecipientDropped`. Replace the selectors only with an
`INhAssistantAlertPolicy` registered through `UseAlertPolicy`; the check applies to what it returns too.
`MaxAlertsPerRun` and `MaxAlertsPerSubjectPerDay` bound the noise. The audit kinds
`AgentAlertRaised`, `AgentAlertResolved`, `AgentAlertDismissed` and `AgentAlertRecipientDropped` carry
identifiers and codes only; the parameters are the application's data and stay in the alert's store.

The run maintenance delivers alerts while the assistant is enabled. It claims the deliveries that are
due, so several instances never send one twice, and checks every recipient again right before sending;
whoever no longer qualifies is left out with the same audit. An alert of a kind delivered immediately,
or of an urgency from `ImmediatelyFrom`, goes out on its own within the maintenance interval. Every
other alert of a person waits for the person's next digest and goes out with their other alerts of that
moment as one notification: its title counts the alerts per urgency ("3 alerts, 1 urgent", in Dutch
"3 attenties, 1 urgent"), it lists at most `NhAssistantLimits.MaxAlertDigestLines` of them, most urgent
first, with "and N more", and in-app it is one thread of its own. A resolved, expired or read alert
leaves a digest that did not go out. `MaxAlertsPerPersonPerDay` bounds what one person receives a day.

The digest falls at the kind's `DailyDigest` time or the time the person chose, on working days (Monday
to Friday) when the kind says `WorkdaysOnly`, in the person's time zone, and stays at that local time
across daylight saving time. The person's zone is what the application's `INhAssistantPersonTimeZones`
gives from its profiles (`UsePersonTimeZones<T>()`), otherwise the application's time zone for alerts:
`NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Alerts:TimeZone` or `ConfigureAlerts`, which the host checks when it starts, and
without it the zone of `UseTimeZone`. A changed digest time applies to the deliveries planned after it.

```csharp
assistant
    .ConfigureAlerts(alerts =>
    {
        alerts.TimeZone = "Europe/Amsterdam";
        alerts.ListUrl = "/alerts";
    })
    .UsePersonTimeZones<ProfileTimeZones>()
    .AddAlertChannel<MailAlertChannel>();
```

A notification goes out through Web Push, with the assistant's browser subscriptions and the person's
one push switch, which stops alerts as it stops proposals, showing the title only unless the kind says
`PushShows(TitleAndText)`; through the in-app notifications of `INhUserNotificationSink`, linking to
`ListUrl`; and through every `INhAssistantAlertChannel` the application adds with `AddAlertChannel`,
such as e-mail, which receives an `NhAssistantAlertMessage` with the texts in the person's culture. A
channel that fails or throws never stops the others; when every channel fails, the delivery is tried
again a few times. Give the push worker the same list as `push.alertsUrl` and open it from
`NhAssistantPushService.openAlerts$`, which a click on a notification of alerts emits.

A person's choices live in the one preference model of the assistant (`AssistantNotificationPreference`),
per kind: muted, the digest time and whether Web Push and the in-app notifications deliver it, as far as
the kind's `PersonMayChange` allows. A `Required` kind is never muted, also when a stored choice says so.
A muted kind, a delivery over the daily limit and a title that fails are withheld
(`NhAssistantAlertDeliveryStatuses.Withheld` with `NhAssistantAlertWithholdReasons`); the alert stays in
the person's list. People read and change only their own choices with `GET` and `PUT notifications`
(`timeZone` and `alertKinds`, `pushEnabled` optional); a change a kind does not allow is refused with
`400` and an `assistant-notification-*` code of `NhAssistantErrorCodes`, and changes nothing.

Alerts add the `AssistantAlert`, `AssistantAlertDelivery` and `AssistantNotificationPreference` tables:
apply the `Alerts` and `NotificationPreferences` migrations of the SQL Server or PostgreSQL assistant
storage before raising the first alert. Everything is opt-in; an application without alert kinds sees
no change.

### The subject's members, resolving by omission and revalidation

`NhAssistantAlertRecipients.SubjectMembers(minRole)` chooses the subject's members with at least that
role, as its resolver lists them when the alert is raised, such as `SubjectMembers(NhAiSubjectRole.Participant)`
for the people who work on it, so the rules name nobody themselves. Combine it with the other selectors
with `Or`; two member selectors ask the lower role (`MinimumMemberRole`). The role is checked live as
Reader is: for a kind whose selectors are only members, the check at delivery and at reading asks that
role, so a member who dropped below it gets nothing more and no longer reads the alert
(`NhAssistantAlertDropReasons.BelowMinimumRole`), and one who lost access gets nothing either. Combined
with another selector, or under an `INhAssistantAlertPolicy`, the person may have been chosen for another
reason, so the check asks Reader, as for the other recipients.

A kind declared with `ResolveWhenNotRaised()` resolves by omission: when an agent's rules finish a run
on a subject with `Done`, also without alerts, the agent's open alerts of the kind about that subject
whose key the result did not raise are resolved, their waiting deliveries are taken back and the audit
records `AgentAlertResolved` with `not-raised` (`NhAssistantAlertCodes.NotRaised`). Raise what applies
now every round and let the platform close what no longer does. Only the run's own subject and the
alerts the agent raised last count: alerts about another subject, about the whole application
(`nh-system`, whose runs resolve only explicitly), of another agent, or that the application's code
raised again since, are left alone, and an alert the result raised but the platform refused, such as
over a limit, counts as raised. A run whose rules throw, raise a kind the agent does not list, hand
over to the model or a skill, or are cancelled resolves nothing by omission, and a shadow run touches
only shadow alerts. One run resolves at most `NhAssistantAlertLimits.MaxRevalidatedAlerts` alerts per
kind this way.

Revalidation (FB87-10) is an explicit call. A kind declares its check in code with `Revalidate<TCheck>()`:
an `INhAssistantAlertCheck` from the application's services, resolved in a scope of its own per alert,
that reads the alert's kind, subject, key and parameters (`NhAssistantAlertCheckContext`) and returns
`StillValid` or `Resolve` (`NhAssistantAlertValidity`). After its change committed, the application calls
`INhAssistantAlerts.RevalidateAsync(subject)`, as it revalidates proposals; nothing revalidates by itself,
so a change the application does not report waits for the next round, the expiry or an explicit
resolve. One call checks at most `MaxRevalidatedAlerts` open alerts of the subject, live before shadow
and each the oldest first, and returns an `NhAssistantAlertRevalidationResult`: the alerts it resolved
(`NhAssistantResolvedAlert`, audited as `AgentAlertResolved` with `revalidated`), how many it checked,
how many checks failed and whether more were left. Alerts of kinds without a check stay as they are,
an alert raised again while its check ran stays open with its new content, and a check that throws
leaves its alert open and is logged with the exception's type only, while the other checks go on.

```csharp
assistant.AddAlertKind("project-due-today", kind => kind
    .DisplayName("app.alerts.project-due-today")
    .Title((culture, parameters) => Texts.Format("ProjectDueToday", culture, parameters["project"]))
    .Recipients(NhAssistantAlertRecipients.SubjectResponsible
        .Or(NhAssistantAlertRecipients.SubjectMembers(NhAiSubjectRole.Participant)))
    .ResolveWhenNotRaised()
    .Revalidate<ProjectDueTodayCheck>());

// Where the change commits, for example in the consumer of the task's event:
await alerts.RevalidateAsync(new NhAiSubjectRef("project", projectId.ToString("D")), cancellationToken);
```

### A person's alerts: the API and the components

`MapNewHeapAssistant` maps a person's side of alerts with the access policy of the assistant
endpoints, and each endpoint reads only the caller's own deliveries. `GET alerts` lists them the most
recently raised first, paged as the approval inbox pages (`page`, `itemsPerPage` up to 100), with the
title and text written in the caller's language, the kind and its name key, the urgency (`info`,
`warning`, `urgent`, `NhAssistantAlertUrgencyNames`), the subject with its parent and their links, and
the caller's state as `status` (`NhAssistantAlertListStatuses`): `unread` or `read` while the alert is
open, `resolved` or `expired` once it closed, `dismissed` once the caller dismissed it. A delivery that was
withheld from the caller's channels, such as for a kind they muted, is `unread` with `isWithheld` and its
`withheldReason`; the badge does not count a muted one. Filter with
`status` (one of those, or `open` and `closed`), `kind`, `subjectType` with `subjectId` and `urgency`;
without a status the list shows every alert the caller did not dismiss. `grouped=true` groups by the
parent the subject's resolver names, as the inbox groups. `GET alerts/summary` gives a badge its
unread count in total and per urgency. `POST alerts/{id}/read` and `POST alerts/{id}/dismiss` are
idempotent and return the alert as the list now shows it; a read delivery that still waits for a
digest is not sent, and the first dismissal is audited as `AgentAlertDismissed`, with the user who
impersonates in an impersonation session. Every alert passes the recipient check again with the
caller's tenant when it is read, so a person who lost access to a subject no longer reads its stored
text: it leaves the list and the counts, and its id answers `404 assistant-alert-not-found`, as do
another person's alerts. A malformed filter answers `400 assistant-alert-filter-invalid`.

In Angular, `@newheap/platform-ai-chat` shows the list with `nh-assistant-alerts`
(`NhAssistantAlertsComponent`): grouped by default, `density: 'compact'` for one row per alert, read
and dismiss in place, resolved and expired alerts shown as such, and `openSubject` with the subject
and its link, which the host routes; the component never navigates. `NhAssistantAlertBadgeService`
gives the shell its badge: call `watch()` where the badge shows and the function it returns when it
no longer does; it reads the counts on load, on focus and visibility, every five minutes while the page
is visible and after the person's own actions. `nh-assistant-notification-preferences`
(`NhAssistantNotificationPreferencesComponent`) shows the push switch of `NhAssistantPushService`, the
person's time zone and per kind what the kind lets them change, and saves through `PUT notifications`.
`NhAssistantApiService` has `getAlerts`, `getAlertSummary`, `markAlertRead`, `dismissAlert` and
`updateNotificationPreferences`; `provideNhAssistantMockApi` serves all of it from the scenario's
`alerts` without a server.

```typescript
// The shell: a bell with the unread count, coloured by the highest urgency.
readonly alertBadge = inject(NhAssistantAlertBadgeService);
private readonly release = this.alertBadge.watch();

// The alerts page: the host routes the subject of an opened alert.
openSubject(target: AlertSubjectTarget): void {
  void this.router.navigateByUrl(target.link ?? `/projects/${target.subjectId}`);
}
```

### The administration of alert kinds

A kind's recipients, texts, urgency and limits are code; its delivery choices may be data. Besides a
person's own choices, an administrator switches a kind off and changes its default delivery, within the
bounds its code sets with `AdministratorMayChange` (`NhAssistantAlertAdminChoices`): `SwitchOff`, and
for the delivery `DigestTimes` (immediately or in digests, and the times of day of the digests),
`WorkdaysOnly`, `ImmediatelyFrom` and `QuietHours`. By default a kind allows `All`; `Required()` takes
`SwitchOff` away, so a required kind is never off, also when a stored setting says so, and `None` keeps
the kind as its code declares it. Declare the bounds where a change would break what the kind is for.

```csharp
assistant.AddAlertKind("project-due-today", kind => kind
    // ...
    .Delivery(delivery => delivery.DailyDigest(new TimeOnly(7, 30)).WorkdaysOnly())
    // An administrator may switch it off and move its digest; recipients and texts stay code.
    .AdministratorMayChange(NhAssistantAlertAdminChoices.SwitchOff | NhAssistantAlertAdminChoices.Delivery));
```

`MapNewHeapAssistant` maps the administration with the admin policy. `GET admin/alert-kinds` lists every
registered kind with what its code allows (`administratorMayChange`), the code's delivery
(`codeDelivery`), the administrator's `settings` with their `version`, and what applies now (`enabled`
and `delivery`), with the numbers of the kind's alerts raised in the period (`from` and `to`, the last
30 days by default, at most 366): `raised`, and per delivery to a person `delivered`, `read`, `dismissed`,
`resolvedBeforeReading`, `withheld` and of those `muted`; and for shadow alerts per agent `wouldHaveSent`.
The numbers cover what the store keeps until `AlertRetention` purges closed alerts.
`PUT admin/alert-kinds/{id}` takes the complete settings, `enabled` and a `delivery` (or `null` for the
code's) with `mode` (`immediately` or `daily-digest`), one to four `digestTimes` as `HH:mm`,
`workdaysOnly`, `immediatelyFrom` and `quietHours` (`start` and `end`), with `expectedVersion` and an
optional `reason`. A change the code does not allow is refused with `400` and
`assistant-alert-kind-switch-off-not-allowed` or `assistant-alert-kind-delivery-not-allowed`, a malformed
delivery with `assistant-alert-kind-delivery-invalid`, both with the parts as field errors; a stale version
answers `409 assistant-version-conflict` and an unknown kind `404 assistant-alert-kind-unknown`. A value
that repeats the code's is accepted, and a delivery equal to the code's is stored as the code's, so the
kind keeps following its code. Every change is the settings' next version in `AssistantAlertKindSetting`
and is audited as `AdminAlertKindChanged` with the names of the settings that changed
(`ChangedFields`), never their values or the reason.

What applies is one effective delivery per kind: the code's merged with the settings the code allows,
read on every host for the next alert that is raised or delivered. The digest scheduler, the delivery
and `GET` and `PUT notifications` use it, and a person's own digest time, mute and channels apply on top
of it. A kind that is off raises nothing: `RaiseAsync` and a rule's alert are refused with
`assistant-alert-kind-off`, nothing is recorded or updated and the run goes on; its open alerts still
resolve, by key, by omission or by revalidation, and expire; a delivery of it that still waits is
withheld as `kind-off` and stays in the person's list without counting in the badge; and a person's
preferences leave it out. Switching it on again lets the next raise plan the withheld deliveries again.
`nh-assistant-admin` shows all of it in its Alerts section (`NhAssistantAdminAlertKindsComponent`), with a
switch and the delivery editable where the code allows it; `NhAssistantAdminApiService` has
`getAlertKinds` and `updateAlertKind`, and `provideNhAssistantMockApi` serves an example view.

### Alerts from an agent's model (FB87-9)

An agent's language model raises an alert only through a template that its kind declares in code
with `RaisedByModel`, and only once an administrator switched it on for the agent. Free text of the
model is never an alert: the model chooses one of the kinds it is offered and fills that kind's typed
parameters, which `NhAssistantAlertModelTemplateBuilder` declares, each required: `Choice` from a fixed
list, `WholeNumber` between bounds, `Date` as `yyyy-MM-dd` and `Text` of at most
`NhAssistantAlertLimits.MaxModelTextLength` characters. `Describe` tells the model when the kind
applies; `Key` names the parameters whose values tell the kind's alerts about one subject apart, and the
platform derives the key from the kind, the subject and those values, so the same values update one
open alert and a person who dismissed it hears again only when they change. Write the kind's title and
text from these parameters only, and prefer a choice or a number to a text.

```csharp
assistant
    .AddAlertKind("project-deliverable-due", kind => kind
        .DisplayName("app.alerts.project-deliverable-due")
        .Title((culture, parameters) => Texts.Format("DeliverableDue", culture, parameters["deliverable"], parameters["daysLeft"]))
        .Recipients(NhAssistantAlertRecipients.SubjectResponsible)
        .RaisedByModel(template => template
            .Describe("A deliverable of the project is due within 14 days and its work is not done.")
            .Text("deliverable", "The deliverable's name, without a file extension.", 80)
            .Date("deadline", "The deliverable's deadline.")
            .WholeNumber("daysLeft", "The days left until the deadline.", 0, 14)
            .Choice("work", "How far its work is.", "not-started", "in-progress")
            .Key("deliverable", "deadline")))
    .ConfigureAgent("deadline-reviewer", agent => agent.Alerts("project-deliverable-due"));
```

A run's model is offered the platform tool `raise_alert` (`assistant.alert.raise`) only for the kinds its
agent lists with `Alerts(...)` that declare a template and whose switch for the agent is shadow or live,
and only in the agent's own run on one subject: never in a person's chat, a person's turn in a thread,
a consultation or a run on the whole application (`nh-system`), which has no person responsible and no
members to warn. Its input is the kind and the parameters, nothing else: the subject is the run's own and
the recipients are the kind's, checked as every alert's recipients are. The values are untrusted, since
the model may have read them in a document an attacker wrote, so the platform checks every one before
anything is stored and refuses with `assistant-alert-parameter-invalid` and the parameter and reason
(`NhAssistantAlertParameterErrors`), never the value: a value outside its choices, bounds or date, an
unknown or missing parameter, an argument that names recipients or a subject, a text that is too long,
and a text with a link (a URL, a scheme such as `mailto:`, a `www.` address, an IP address or a word with
a dot between letters such as `example.com` or `report.pdf`, which mail clients and phones turn into
links), with markup (`<`, `>`, brackets, braces, a backtick or an HTML entity) or with a control, format or
private-use character. A kind the tool does not offer is refused with `assistant-alert-kind-not-offered`.
The alert is then raised as a rule's: `MaxAlertsPerRun` counts the run's alerts, `MaxAlertsPerSubjectPerDay`
the subject's, a kind that is off is refused with `assistant-alert-kind-off` and a paused agent raises
nothing. The result tells the model only whether the alert was recorded and whether it was new, updated or
unchanged, never whom it reaches, and reads the same in shadow. The alert stores that the model raised or
last updated it (`AssistantAlert.RaisedByModel`), `AgentAlertRaised` carries `AlertRaisedByModel`, `GET
alerts` returns `raisedByModel` and `nh-assistant-alerts` labels it "Raised by AI"; render its title and
text as plain text only, in every channel of the application too.

Roll the model out per agent and kind as running without approval is rolled out (FB82), with
`INhAssistantAlertModelSwitches` behind the admin policy: `GET admin/agents/{id}/alert-model` lists the
kinds the agent lists that declare a template, with when they apply, their parameters and the switch,
and `PUT admin/agents/{id}/alert-kinds/{kindId}/model` switches it with `mode` and `expectedVersion`. A
switch starts off, goes to shadow first, where the model's alerts are shadow alerts that reach nobody and
count as `wouldHaveSent` in `GET admin/alert-kinds`, and only from shadow live, where they reach the kind's
recipients; off before live answers `409 assistant-alert-model-shadow-first`, a kind the agent's model cannot
raise `409 assistant-alert-model-not-allowed`. Versions are append-only (`AssistantAgentAlertModelSwitch`,
`GET .../model/versions`), every change is audited as `AdminAlertModelSwitchChanged` with the mode and
version, never the reason, and applies to the next run on every host. A switch applies to the template it
was made for: a kind whose template changed reads as off until it is switched again, first in shadow. A
shadow agent's or shadow run's alerts stay shadow alerts whatever the switch says, and a shadow variant has
no switch of its own. `nh-assistant-admin` shows the switches on the agent's Rollout tab, explaining each
step before it applies. Apply the `AlertModelSwitches` migration of the SQL Server or PostgreSQL assistant
storage before the first switch.

## Avoid

- Raising a proposal, or an application message in a thread, to warn a person about an object.
- Building the text of an alert in one language when it is raised, or putting the text into the key.
- A key that changes every round, such as a timestamp or a count, which warns people every round.
- Resolving every alert of a kind by hand in each round when the kind can `ResolveWhenNotRaised()`, or
  relying on omission for alerts about another subject than the run's or that the application raises.
- Expecting alerts to revalidate on their own after a change; call `RevalidateAsync` where it commits.
- A check that changes data, calls slow services or writes an alert's parameters into its logs.
- Choosing recipients by hand and skipping the platform's check, or naming people who cannot read
  the subject and relying on the application to filter them later.
- Writing parameters, titles or texts into logs or the audit.
- Showing the text on a lock screen (`PushShows(TitleAndText)`) when it may carry confidential data.
- Sending alerts from the application's own job or building a digest from the delivery table; add an
  `INhAssistantAlertChannel` for the application's channel instead.
- A channel that throws for one failed message or writes an alert's texts into its logs.
- Keeping digest times or mutes per person in the application; they are the person's choices in the
  assistant's preferences, which the kind bounds.
- Reading `NhAssistantAlertKind.Delivery` to decide when an alert goes out; an administrator's settings
  change it, so the delivery that applies is the platform's effective one.
- Letting administrators change what must not change: declare `AdministratorMayChange` narrower, or make
  the kind `Required()`, instead of relying on nobody using the switch.
- Sending only `enabled` in `PUT admin/alert-kinds/{id}`: the body is the complete settings, so a missing
  `delivery` resets it to the code's.
- Reading the alert store yourself for a person's list or badge instead of `GET alerts`, which checks
  every alert against the person's access again.
- Navigating from inside the alert list, or polling the summary yourself next to the badge service.
- Letting a model write an alert's text, or a template parameter that is free text where a choice, a
  number or a date fits; a text parameter is the one place where content the model read reaches people.
- Switching the model live without a period in shadow, or switching it on for an agent whose model reads
  content that people outside the subject write without looking at its shadow alerts first.
- Rendering an alert's title or text as HTML or Markdown, in the platform's list or in an application
  channel such as e-mail.

## Verification

Run the rules twice on the same subject and assert one open alert at its first revision; raise it
again with other content, a higher urgency and after `RepeatAfter`, and assert the revision and which
deliveries wait. Dismiss it and assert the person is not planned again until the key changes. Resolve
it and let it expire, then move the application's clock past the retention and assert the maintenance
purged it. Name a person without `Reader`, a person of another division and a person the principal
factory no longer rebuilds, and assert they get no delivery and an `AgentAlertRecipientDropped` audit.
Assert that an unlisted kind fails the run, that a shadow run's alerts reach nobody and that a paused
agent raises nothing. For the delivery, move the application's clock to 07:30 in a person's time zone
and assert one digest per person and digest time with its counts, an immediate alert on its own, a
person in another zone at their own 07:30 and a digest across a change to or from daylight saving time.
Assert that a person who lost `Reader` before the delivery gets nothing, that a muted kind is withheld
and a required one cannot be muted, that a resolved, expired or read alert leaves a waiting digest,
that the daily limit holds, that two dispatchers never send one delivery twice and that a failing
channel does not stop the others. Assert that `PUT notifications` changes only the caller's choices and
refuses what a kind does not allow. Run the store tests on SQL Server and PostgreSQL. SPM-392 is the
executable reference.

For the lifecycle, raise a kind with `SubjectMembers(Participant)` and assert that a member below the
role is not chosen, and that one who dropped below it or lost access gets nothing at delivery and no
longer reads the alert. Run the rules twice on a subject and assert that the second run resolves the
keys it did not raise again with `not-raised`, but no alert about another subject, of a kind without
`ResolveWhenNotRaised`, of the application's code or of a run on the whole application; that a run
whose rules fail, hand over or are cancelled resolves nothing; and that a shadow run touches only
shadow alerts. Revalidate a subject and assert what its check resolved, that a kind without a check
keeps its alerts and that one failing check stops no other, on SQL Server and PostgreSQL.

For the administration, read `GET admin/alert-kinds` and assert each kind's bounds, its code's
delivery and what applies; change a delivery within the bounds and assert the next version, the audit
with the changed settings, the moment the scheduler plans and the default in `GET notifications`;
switch a kind off and assert that raising it is refused with `assistant-alert-kind-off`, that a waiting
delivery is withheld as `kind-off` and that resolving still works. Assert that a required kind, a part
the code does not allow, a malformed delivery and a stale version are refused and save nothing, that the
numbers count each delivery once per period and the shadow alerts per agent, and that people without the
admin policy get `401` or `403`, on SQL Server and PostgreSQL.

For a person's side, read `GET alerts` as the recipient and assert the title in their language, the
subject's link and the groups per parent across pages; mark one read and dismiss one twice and assert
the badge's counts and one `AgentAlertDismissed`. Assert that another person, a person who lost access
to the subject and an impersonation session's origin user list nothing and get `404` for the id, on
SQL Server and PostgreSQL. In Angular, render the list and the notification choices on
`provideNhAssistantMockApi` with an `alerts` scenario.

For the model tool, declare a kind with a template, list it for an agent and assert that the tool is not
offered while the switch is off, for a kind without a template, for a kind the agent does not list and in
a run on the whole application; that live before shadow is refused; that a shadow alert reaches nobody and
a live one only the kind's checked recipients; that a text with a URL, a word such as `example.com`,
markup or a control character, a value outside its choices or bounds, an unknown or missing parameter, a
text that is too long and arguments that name recipients or a subject are refused before anything is
stored; that the same key values update one alert; and that the store, the audit and `GET alerts` mark the
alert as the model's, on SQL Server and PostgreSQL. In Angular, render the Rollout tab on
`provideNhAssistantMockApi` with `admin.alertModel` and the list with an alert that has `raisedByModel`.
